approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecules from score-ranked accepted parents using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It trains a Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process on all accepted observations and chooses a batch from each new offspring pool through correlated posterior function draws. Its atom-replacement move picks any source atom, then applies the inherited aromaticity and valence rules to choose a different element. That move can remove a carbonyl from an otherwise promising amide or carbonyl-containing ring.
approach.novelty: Preserve existing carbonyl groups during atom replacement by choosing the replacement site only among atoms outside C=O pairs. The remaining atom and element substitutions use the Parent's rules, allowing local variants around an intact carbonyl framework. This differs from the completed halogen-site experiment and earlier changes to parent memory or partner choice: it changes the support of one substitution operator, with intact C=O retention as the measurable intermediate effect.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent repeatedly reaches useful aromatic amide, lactam and dicarbonyl families, but replace_atom draws uniformly over every source atom and can replace an existing carbonyl oxygen or carbon. A read-only audit of its complete recorded panel finds that 751 of 7,016 pooled products whose sole realized operation is replace_atom have fewer C=O bonds than their source. Such loss reaches 60 of 589 single-replacement emissions: five of those 60 beat their source, their mean accepted score is 0.272571 and their mean source-relative change is -0.077030. The 525 single-replacement emissions with unchanged carbonyl count have 62 source beats and mean score 0.345113; these groups have different source strengths and are observational, so they do not establish a causal penalty for losing a carbonyl. Four emitted replacements instead increase carbonyl count. The molecular assessment identifies useful carbonyl/amine/aromatic relationships that edits do not consistently preserve, while also showing that bulk carbonyl abundance alone is insufficient. The completed halogen-attachment sibling confirms that a narrow chemical production rule can activate without endpoint benefit: 22 redirected descendants were evaluated and the paired macro mean fell by 0.005165. This Child therefore tests the separate preservation of existing C=O groups in one atom-substitution channel, rather than inferring general chemical or score improvement from motif counts.
hypothesis: Restrict atom-replacement targets to atoms outside existing carbonyl C=O pairs, preserving both carbonyl atoms and their double bond in that operator.

finding_summary.headline: Carbonyls survived replacement, but scores fell and neighboring functional groups still changed
finding_summary.insights: The intervention closes the intended destructive replacement channel, but that channel is not sufficient to explain useful graph evolution. Existing carbonyl atoms and their double bond can survive while adjacent amide-like or ester-like connections change, and subsequent operators still remove some carbonyls. Indeed, thirty-six protected replacements introduced an acyl-halide connection by changing an unprotected neighboring atom, and five of those paths reached evaluation. The sole all-protected case correctly retried through another operator rather than substituting a protected endpoint. The Parent also had five source-beating carbonyl-loss emissions, so motif removal was not uniformly harmful. The negative score result therefore narrows the useful question to which complete functional relationships deserve preservation, rather than carbonyl retention alone. The supplied chemistry reinforces that limit: useful aryl amine and indole-carbonyl families coexist with strained aromatic bridges, oversized repeated assemblies and reactive halogen or peroxide connections, with no specified stereochemistry. In particular, the large seed-0 DRD2 decline accompanies bulkier hydroperoxide-containing chemistry; the experiment does not isolate one structural cause of that decline. The inherited representation issue also reached one evaluated pure-crossover product, outside the replacement channel. Neither unchosen sites nor unselected pool molecules have counterfactual scores, so the observed subgroups cannot establish that allowing a particular omitted replacement would have improved the endpoint.
finding_summary.results: All 12,104 successful replacements on carbonyl-bearing sources preserved every original C=O pair. The protected substitutions reached 11,191 pool descendants and 718 actual evaluated descendants. Among products made by a single replacement, carbonyl loss fell from 751 of 7,016 Parent pool products and sixty of 589 Parent emissions to zero of 7,100 pool products and zero of 526 emissions. This did not preserve the whole functional group: 93 evaluated descendants contain replacements that changed an original carbonyl’s neighboring atom class, including 41 that lost an adjacent nitrogen. Across the full emitted stream, acyl-halide-bearing molecules increased from seventeen to 272. All fifteen task/seed runs completed with 4,350 valid novel submitted offspring and no evaluator invalid or duplicate attempts. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.509621, a paired change of -0.034753. The seed changes were -0.089860, -0.027023 and +0.012624. The mean DRD2 change was -0.146641, while median_2 improved by 0.009198.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and indole carbonyl rings gain locally, but strained aromatic bridges and reactive halogen bonds persist
molecular.overall_character: The complete supplied current and parent trajectories cover every task and seed. Current outputs include compact bridged aryl amides, linked heteroaromatic diones, aryl/basic-amine assemblies, expanded indole-fused carbonyl rings, and fluorinated dione derivatives. Ring and aromatic content are rich: ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9759 to 0.9954, and aromatic-token presence from 0.9368 to 0.9908. These are molecule-level SMILES text readings, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of feasible geometry. Each task has 900 observations including 870 optimizer proposals. Substantial ring systems predominate, but occasional very small fragments and repeated oversized assemblies remain. The more conventional indole carbonyl family provides a plausible chemical direction, while other leaders retain direct N-F or N-Cl bonds, strained aromatic bridges, or reactive alkyl/oxygen-halogen functionality. High-scoring neutral aryl amines are present, so basic centres are not a general missing capability. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout, despite ionizable groups and potentially stereogenic connections. The seed families provide moderate structural diversity, with many variants still concentrated around their respective core arrangements. Relative to the parent, the chemical families change without consistently resolving synthetic plausibility, geometry, or stability.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact methoxy/methyl-substituted aromatic systems with fused or bridged nitrogen-containing rings, an alkene, and an N-fluoro phenylamide. Related molecules add fluorine, hydroxyl, amino, N-N, or oxygen-containing bridge connections. Other seeds produce sulfur-containing fused lactams and extensively annulated nitrogen/carbonyl systems, sometimes with small-ring or difficult bridge topology. Thus the generator already supplies aromatic bulk, heterocycles, and carbonyl functionality: aromatic and ring presence are 0.9621 and 0.9759, with mean SMILES length 45.5. The aryl/carbonyl components are recognizable, but direct fluorination of the amide nitrogen is a distinct stability concern, and the densely connected ring geometry is not validated by the SMILES.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonding on the amide nitrogen is not routine carbon-bound fluorination and raises chemical stability questions.
Several related structures add N-N or N-O connections without improving the leading supplied score.
Dense annulation and bridging complicate synthesis and conformational feasibility, while occasional small fragments discard the useful architecture.
missing_features: Matched ordinary amide-nitrogen alternatives retaining the leading aryl and bridged-ring arrangement are missing from the cited top series.
Less constrained ring connections preserving the productive carbonyl and aromatic relationships are insufficiently represented.
Stereochemically defined substituted bridge variants are absent despite their potentially stereogenic connectivity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy/methyl bridged N-fluoroamide reaches 0.457660. Adding a carbon-bound fluorine or a bridge amino group gives 0.431364; adding hydroxyl gives 0.426006, and replacing a bridge carbon with nitrogen gives 0.429932. These local examples favor the less decorated leading arrangement, rather than indiscriminate addition of polar or halogen groups. Small fragments such as ethene and methane score zero. Final complex annulated structures range from 0.111928 to 0.353532 among the cited examples, so ring complexity by itself is insufficient. The current seed-0 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.446352 while exchanging its bridged N/O-aromatic ketone connection for an N-fluoroamide family. The current seed-1 and seed-2 maxima, 0.403194 and 0.368052, are below their respective parent maxima of 0.412682 and 0.416350. The supplied chemistry therefore does not establish that the N-F bond is needed for the score increase.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family links an alkyl-substituted azaaromatic ring to an N-chlorinated fused dione and a substituted dimethylaminoaryl group. The aryl group contains a benzene-fused oxygen-containing small ring, so the apparent compactness still comes with geometric strain. Some near-leaders also carry an N-chloro-N-methyl arylamine or additional tightly fused ring connections. Elsewhere, particularly in seed-0, much larger assemblies accumulate azaaromatics, carbonyls, unsaturated side chains, and repeated connecting units. Mean SMILES length is 89.1 and maximum 244; aromatic and ring presence are both 0.9862. Final seed-2 molecules combine heteroaromatic diones, arylamides, chlorinated N-alkyl groups, and unusually constrained azaaromatic fragments. Apparent synthesis and stability remain questionable across these different size regimes.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl bonds on cyclic carbonyl nitrogens and arylamines introduce reactive functionality.
The benzene-fused oxygen small ring and other constrained aromatic closures require geometric and synthetic scrutiny.
Large repeated unsaturated/carbonyl assemblies add substantial size and connecting-group complexity without a consistent supplied-score advantage.
Acid chlorides and chlorinated N-alkyl groups appear in late molecules and are not evidence of stable medicinal chemistry.
missing_features: Matched removal of the retained dione N-Cl bond while preserving the leading framework is not demonstrated.
Ordinary ring replacements for the benzene-fused oxygen small ring and tightly constrained azaaromatic fragments are underrepresented.
Compact stable connecting groups are insufficiently represented relative to repeated large assemblies or highly annulated alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact dimethylaminoaryl/azaaryl/N-chloro dione scores 0.616746. A matched pair exchanging the aryl N-methyl-N-chloro substituent for dimethylamino ties at 0.615854, so that particular N-Cl bond has no demonstrated local score benefit. Related side-chain and annulation variants cluster near the same score; a more rearranged leader without direct N-chlorination reaches 0.613820. Small fragments, including ethane and chlorodimethylamine, remain at the 0.5 floor. The seed-0 oversized, extensively unsaturated assembly peaks at 0.602368, below the compact seed-1 family, so more size or repeated functionality is not a general solution. The parent's best was 0.632470 in an oxygen-halogen/peroxide-containing polycycle. The current leading family changes that chemistry to N-chlorination and an oxygen small ring, rather than demonstrating chemically benign replacements throughout. A final acid-chloride dione scores 0.548901, below the more complete final arylamide structures around 0.59.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-2 molecules combine substituted aromatic groups, a tertiary amine, an aminochlorophenyl group, and cyclobutane or cyclopentane connections. Their most distinctive feature is a highly compressed carbon bridge across one aromatic ring, bearing both the tertiary amine and a chloromethyl substituent. This is not simply an ordinary fused saturated ring: the short aromatic bridge imposes serious geometric questions. Neighboring leaders use azetidine, pyrrolidine, or more bridged amine connections; seed-1 instead yields a fused aryl/amine system with an exocyclic alkene and chlorinated saturated carbon. Aromatic and ring presence are 0.9874 and 0.9931, and halogen presence is 0.9954. Mean SMILES length is 82.9 and maximum 224, partly reflecting a much larger, less successful seed-0 population with hydroperoxide-containing aryl ketone/amine assemblies.
liabilities: The very short carbon bridge across an aromatic ring creates substantial strain and aromatic-geometry concerns.
Chloromethyl, sulfenyl chloride, and halogenated saturated amine variants add reactivity concerns in individual leaders.
Some much larger outputs carry hydroperoxide groups and multiple connecting units despite lower supplied scores.
Neutral amine drawings and unspecified ring stereochemistry do not establish an accessible bound or solution conformation.
missing_features: Ordinary aromatic-to-amine connections preserving the leading group spacing without the compressed carbon bridge are absent from the cited top series.
Stable replacements for the chloromethyl substituent and other reactive peripheral groups are not established in a matched series.
Defined stereochemical and conformational identities of the bridged and substituted saturated rings are missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propyl-substituted aromatic-bridge/tertiary-amine/cyclobutane molecule reaches 0.995245; shortening propyl to ethyl gives 0.993619, and expanding the cyclobutane connection to cyclopentane in the ethyl series gives 0.992313. These are close local preferences within a complete aryl/amine architecture. A related final molecule whose aminoaryl region becomes an expanded nonaromatic ring scores 0.311185, compared with 0.992074 for its cited aromatic relative. Low N-sulfonyl cyclic amines and acid/amide derivatives score 0.000338-0.000973, showing that aromaticity, halogens, or nitrogen presence alone are insufficient. The current seed-2 maximum is slightly above the parent's 0.991404 and changes the parent's aryl/amine-diazaring arrangement to a different highly constrained bridge. Seed-1 rises from 0.951235 to 0.993101, while seed-0 falls from 0.990833 to 0.505204 with bulkier hydroperoxide-containing chemistry. No comparison isolates the strained aromatic bridge as a chemically necessary feature.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is comparatively conventional: an alkyl/ethoxy/chloro-substituted phenyl group is attached to an expanded nitrogen-containing carbonyl ring fused to indole. The best contains lactam/urea-like carbonyl connections and N-methyl groups; a close relative replaces an N-methyl connection with a methyl-bearing carbon, giving a ketone/amide arrangement. The indole NH provides a donor alongside the carbonyl acceptors, while the aryl alkyl and ethoxy groups contribute hydrophobic surface. Other seeds produce expanded aryl carbonyl rings and fused N-methyl lactams. Ring and aromatic presence are 0.9954 and 0.9908, halogen presence is 0.2092, and mean SMILES length is 59.9. These leaders avoid exotic heteroatom-halogen bonds, although closure and conformation of the expanded ring still require a credible synthesis.
liabilities: The expanded ring can be synthetically and conformationally demanding even though its individual bond types are conventional.
Multiple aromatic groups, alkyl chains, and ethers create substantial hydrophobic surface; no solubility or exposure measurement is supplied.
Late duplication, direct O-Cl substitution, and other unusual rearrangements remain present below the leading score region.
missing_features: More compact or independently connected alternatives preserving the indole, aryl, and carbonyl relationships are insufficiently represented.
Matched variations that reduce expanded-ring conformational complexity without losing the productive functional-group arrangement are missing.
Stereochemical identities of the methyl-bearing carbon and substituted-ring analogues remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The lactam/urea-like leader scores 0.243961, versus 0.240613 for the methyl-bearing carbon analogue. Shortening its ethoxy group to methoxy gives 0.228781. In the carbon analogue, extending aryl propyl to butyl gives 0.232283 and adding a thiol gives 0.231592, both below 0.240613. The gradient supports a particular intact aryl/indole/carbonyl arrangement rather than uniformly increasing size or adding heteroatoms. Small aminomethylamine and methane fragments score zero, while a large doubled final assembly scores 0.163019. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.210377, changing from a quinoline-linked expanded nitrogen/carbonyl ring to the indole-fused family. It also exceeds the parent's overall best of 0.224057, although these different scaffolds do not isolate which individual feature is responsible.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-0 molecule is a nitrogen-rich fused dione attached to a hydroxymethylphenyl group and a brominated N-fluoroazetidine side chain. Direct N-F bonds occur on the cyclic carbonyl nitrogens as well as the azetidine nitrogen. A close high-scoring relative expands the nitrogen/carbonyl ring. Seed-2 provides a different family of N-methyl aromatic diones bearing fluoromethyl, fluoroalkyl ketone, fluoroalkoxy, or direct O-F/acyl-fluoride functionality. Its high-scoring open-chain relative replaces an aryl region with a conjugated fluorinated chain that still bears an O-F-containing substituent. Aromatic and ring presence are 0.9368 and 0.977, with mean SMILES length 54.6. Compact conventional-looking carbonyl cores are present, but their peripheral bonding and some ring constructions remain problematic.
liabilities: Direct N-F and O-F bonds are chemically distinct from ordinary carbon-bound fluorination.
Acyl fluoride and fluorinated ketone groups have different reactivity; their presence should not be collapsed into one fluorine feature.
The brominated N-fluoroazetidine combines ring strain with reactive nitrogen and carbon substitution.
Late conjugated chains and highly constrained ring rearrangements introduce additional stability or geometric questions.
missing_features: Matched ordinary N-substitution alternatives around the leading dione and azetidine are absent from the cited top series.
The demonstrated favorable carbon-bound-fluorine alternatives have not been extended into a complete stable peripheral-group series.
Compact independently connected structures are underrepresented relative to ring rearrangements, reactive fluorination, and repeated dione assemblies.
Stereochemically specified brominated azetidine and other saturated-ring variants are missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The multiply N-fluorinated azetidine/dione leader scores 0.511498, and an expanded-ring relative scores 0.497894. The conjugated-chain dione scores 0.496312. Crucially, a more conventional aryl dione with carbon-bound fluorine in a fluoromethoxy group and fluoroalkyl ketone scores 0.469278. The otherwise matched direct O-F analogue scores 0.453462, and the otherwise matched acyl-fluoride analogue also scores 0.453462. Inserting carbon between oxygen and fluorine, or between the carbonyl and fluorine, therefore improves these supplied local scores while removing the corresponding reactive bond type. Large repeated dione assemblies score as low as 4.20e-40, so duplication is strongly disfavored in those observed examples. The current maximum is below the parent's 0.584558 aryl dione/aminomethyl/fluoromethyl maximum, which lacked the current leader's combination of direct N-F bonds and brominated azetidine. Those bonds are consequently not established as a required chemical solution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Direct N-F and N-Cl bonds occur in several leading families, with O-F and acyl fluoride in related structures. A matched N-chloro-to-dimethylamino substitution ties at 0.615854. Separately, replacing direct O-F or acyl fluoride with the corresponding carbon-separated fluorine arrangement raises a supplied local score from 0.453462 to 0.469278.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable alternatives to heteroatom-halogen and acyl-halide bonds are not explored consistently around productive scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable local replacements that preserve the surrounding aryl/carbonyl arrangement and approximately preserve size accessible throughout generation. Use current objective feedback to compare those alternatives rather than treating a reactive bond in a leading molecule as required chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring molecules include compressed carbon bridges across aromatic rings, benzene-fused oxygen small rings, and other highly constrained aromatic fragments. Ring-token presence is already high, while a relatively conventional expanded indole/carbonyl family supplies a different route to meaningful score movement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish feasible ring architecture from an accepted aromatic closure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support alternative bridge lengths, ring sizes, saturation patterns, and fusion connections that preserve useful substituent relationships. Treat aromatic valence validity and ring closure as incomplete evidence of geometric or synthetic feasibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied proposals include very small zero-scoring fragments and large repeated assemblies. One population reaches SMILES length 244, whereas its leading family is much more compact; a doubled indole/carbonyl assembly scores 0.163019, and repeated aromatic diones can score near zero.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful molecular architecture is inconsistently preserved during size changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable controlled simplification, removal of duplicated units, and bounded connecting-group edits while retaining the informative core. Let observed local structural comparisons determine whether extra size is useful instead of repeatedly losing the core or duplicating it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All digest populations have zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence. Cited bridged amines, substituted saturated rings, methyl-bearing carbonyl-ring analogues, and brominated azetidines support stereochemical distinctions that the strings leave unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity and accessible conformation remain unresolved as substituted rings become more complex.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemistry through structural changes and make valid local stereoisomer alternatives available when new centres arise. Pair those alternatives with credible ring geometry and current scoring feedback rather than assuming unspecified connectivity represents one accessible structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Close arylamide, aryl-amine, and indole/carbonyl analogues show interpretable local preferences, but many other proposals simultaneously change ring topology, reactive bonds, and size. The conventional indole/carbonyl series and the carbon-bound-fluorine aryl dione show useful chemistry without every liability found in neighboring leaders.
transferable_gaps.gap: Independent stable arrangements of productive functional groups are underrepresented relative to decoration of complex current families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched changes to aryl position, carbonyl connection, amine spacing, and ring topology while retaining the rest of the molecule. Provide synthetically credible alternative connections so feedback can distinguish useful functionality from incidental strain or reactivity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
